name.en: Mini zaatar manakish

en: Half cup wholewheat flour
Half tsp instant yeast
2 tbsp dried zaatar mix
1 tsp olive oil
Warm water, a little salt
Knead the flour, yeast and salt with warm water
Let it rest 45 minutes
Roll into a round and brush with oil and zaatar
Bake 12 minutes at 220°C

name.en: Foul and egg wrap

en: 1 saj bread or wholewheat tortilla
Half cup mashed cooked fava beans
1 egg
Chopped tomato and cucumber
Lemon juice, cumin, salt
Mash the beans with the lemon, cumin and salt
Fry the egg sunny-side up or scrambled
Spread the beans on the bread and top with the egg
Add the tomato and cucumber, then roll

name.en: Baked Mini Manakish bi Jibn (Cheese Manakish)

en: Ready-made whole-wheat bread dough 80 g
Low-fat cottage cheese 60 g
Low-fat grated mozzarella 30 g
A pinch of dried thyme
Chopped fresh mint for garnish (optional)
1 tsp olive oil
Divide the dough into 2 small balls, roll into thin circles.
Mix the cottage cheese, mozzarella and thyme in a bowl.
Spread the cheese mixture evenly over each dough circle.
Brush the edges with olive oil, bake at 220°C for 12-15 minutes until golden on the bottom and the cheese is cooked, garnish with mint if desired and serve hot.

name.en: Hummus Breakfast Plate with Olive Oil and Pine Nuts

en: Canned chickpeas, drained, 200 g
Tahini 1 tbsp and lemon juice 2 tbsp
1 small crushed garlic clove and salt
Olive oil 1 tsp and toasted pine nuts 1 tsp for garnish
A pinch of paprika for garnish
Baladi or whole-wheat bread to serve (optional)
Blend the chickpeas with the tahini, lemon juice, garlic and salt in a food processor until a smooth, creamy mixture forms.
Add a little water if the texture is too thick and continue blending.
Pour into a serving plate and make a well in the centre with the back of a spoon.
Pour the olive oil into the well, sprinkle with toasted pine nuts and paprika, and serve with bread if desired.

name.en: Shakshuka Shami (Levantine Eggs in Tomato Sauce)

en: 2 eggs
2 medium tomatoes, diced
Red bell pepper, diced, and chopped onion
1 crushed garlic clove and ground cumin half a tsp
A pinch of sweet paprika and 1 tsp olive oil
Salt, black pepper and pita bread to serve (optional)
Heat the oil in a pan, brown the onion and bell pepper for 4 minutes until softened.
Add the garlic, tomatoes, cumin, paprika, salt and black pepper, cook 8-10 minutes until the sauce thickens.
Make two small wells in the sauce and crack the eggs into them.
Cover the pan and cook 5-6 minutes until the whites are set and the yolks remain soft, serve hot with pita bread if desired.

name.en: Akkawi Cheese Breakfast Plate with Za'atar and Tomato

en: Low-salt Akkawi cheese 80 g
Medium tomato, sliced, and cucumber, sliced, 150 g total
Dried thyme (zaatar) 1 tbsp and olive oil 1 tsp
5 green olives (optional)
Pita or whole-wheat bread, 1 slice (40 g)
Fresh mint for garnish (optional)
Arrange the Akkawi cheese in the centre of a serving plate.
Arrange the tomato and cucumber slices around it.
Mix the thyme with the olive oil and pour it over the cheese.
Add the olives if desired, serve with the bread, and garnish with fresh mint if desired.

name.en: Baked Kaak bi Simsim (Sesame Ring Bread)

en: Whole-wheat flour 70 g
Warm water about 40 ml and a pinch of instant yeast
Brown sugar half a tsp and a pinch of salt
1 tsp oil for the dough
Sesame seeds 20 g for coating
1 beaten egg for brushing (optional)
Mix the flour with the warm water, yeast, brown sugar, salt and oil gradually until a soft, cohesive dough forms, let it rest 30 minutes.
Shape into a long rope, then tie into a ring, press the ends together to seal.
Brush with the beaten egg if desired, dip in the sesame seeds to coat fully.
Arrange on a lined tray, bake at 200°C for 18-20 minutes until golden and crisp.

name.en: Labneh and Cucumber Wrap with Mint

en: Low-fat labneh 80 g
Cucumber, cut into thin sticks, and cherry tomatoes, halved
Chopped fresh mint and a pinch of dried thyme
Thin pita or whole-wheat bread, 1 loaf (60 g)
Olive oil 1 tsp
A little salt
Mix the labneh with the mint, thyme and a little salt.
Spread the labneh mixture over the bread.
Arrange the cucumber and cherry tomatoes over the labneh, drizzle with olive oil.
Roll it up tightly into a cylinder, cut in half and serve.

name.en: Baked Mini Manakish bi Lahmeh (Meat-Topped Manakish)

en: Ready-made whole-wheat bread dough 80 g
Lean minced beef 60 g
Diced tomato and chopped onion
Mixed spice half a tsp and pomegranate molasses 1 tsp (optional)
Salt and black pepper
Chopped parsley for garnish
Mix the minced meat with the tomato, onion, mixed spice, pomegranate molasses if desired, salt and black pepper until combined.
Divide the dough into 2 small balls, roll into thin circles.
Spread the meat mixture evenly over each dough circle to cover most of the disc.
Bake at 220°C for 15-18 minutes until the meat is cooked and the pastry turns golden, garnish with parsley and serve hot.

name.en: Baked Halloumi and Tomato Breakfast Plate

en: Low-salt halloumi cheese, sliced, 100 g
2 medium tomatoes, sliced
A pinch of dried thyme and 1 tsp olive oil
Pita or whole-wheat bread, 1 slice (40 g)
Fresh mint for garnish (optional)
Black pepper
Arrange the halloumi slices on a lined tray.
Bake at 220°C for 10-12 minutes, turning halfway, until golden on the outside.
Arrange the tomato slices around the halloumi on a serving plate.
Sprinkle with thyme, olive oil and black pepper, serve with the bread and garnish with mint if desired.

name.en: Freekeh with chicken

en: 150 g chicken breast, cubed
100 g cooked freekeh
1 onion, 2 garlic cloves
Seven-spice mix, cinnamon
1 tsp oil, toasted almonds to garnish
Brown the chicken with onion and garlic 6 minutes
Add the spice and a cup of water, cook 10 minutes
Add the cooked freekeh and stir through
Serve hot, scattered with toasted almonds

name.en: Fattoush with toasted bread

en: Half a loaf of bread, cubed
Lettuce, tomato, cucumber, radish
Spring onion, parsley, mint
Lemon juice, pomegranate molasses
1 tsp olive oil, sumac
Toast the bread cubes in the oven until crisp
Chop all the vegetables small
Mix the lemon juice, molasses, oil and sumac
Toss the vegetables with the bread and dressing just before serving

name.en: Mjadara (Lentils and Rice with Caramelized Onions)

en: Boiled brown lentils, drained, 100 g
White rice 70 g
2 large onions, thinly sliced
Ground cumin half a tsp and water 300 ml
1 tsp olive oil and salt
Simple cucumber and tomato salad to serve (optional)
Brown the onion in a dry pan over medium-low heat 15-18 minutes, stirring, until it turns dark and sweet.
Remove half the onion for garnish, leave the other half in the pan.
Add the lentils, rice, cumin, water and salt to the pan, cover and simmer 18-20 minutes until the rice is fully cooked and absorbs the water.
Drizzle with olive oil, garnish with the remaining browned onion, and serve with the cucumber and tomato salad if desired.

name.en: Shish Tawook (Grilled Chicken Skewers) with Rice

en: Chicken breast, cubed, 140 g
Low-fat Greek yogurt 2 tbsp and lemon juice 1 tbsp
2 crushed garlic cloves and paprika half a tsp
Salt, black pepper and 1 tsp oil
Wooden skewers soaked in water
Cooked white rice 110 g
Mix the yogurt, lemon juice, garlic, paprika, salt and black pepper to make the marinade.
Marinate the chicken in it and let it sit at least 30 minutes or overnight in the fridge.
Thread onto the wooden skewers and brush with oil.
Grill under the broiler or in a 220°C oven for 15-18 minutes, turning halfway, until fully cooked, and serve with the rice.

name.en: Kousa Mahshi (Stuffed Zucchini with Rice and Meat)

en: Small zucchini, hollowed out, 5 pieces (400 g)
Egyptian or short-grain rice 60 g
Lean minced beef 80 g
Diced tomato and 1 crushed garlic clove
Mixed spice half a tsp, salt and black pepper
Light vegetable stock or tomato water 300 ml
Mix the rice with the minced meat, tomato, garlic, mixed spice, salt and black pepper.
Stuff the hollowed zucchini with the mixture up to about two-thirds full to leave room for expansion.
Arrange them snugly in a pot, side by side.
Pour the stock over them to nearly cover, cover and simmer 40-45 minutes until the rice and zucchini are fully cooked, and serve warm.

name.en: Musakhan Chicken with Sumac and Onions

en: Chicken breast, sliced, 140 g
2 large onions, thinly sliced
Ground sumac 1 tbsp and 1 tsp olive oil
Toasted pine nuts 1 tbsp (optional)
Thin pita or whole-wheat bread, 1 loaf (60 g)
Salt and black pepper
Brown the onion in a dry pan over medium-low heat 15 minutes, stirring, until soft and slightly golden.
Add the chicken, sumac, salt and black pepper, cook 8-10 minutes until the chicken is fully cooked.
Spread the bread on a tray, distribute the chicken and onion mixture over it, drizzle with olive oil.
Bake at 200°C for 8-10 minutes until the edges of the bread are golden, garnish with pine nuts if desired and serve.

name.en: Baked Sayadieh (Levantine Fish with Spiced Rice)

en: White fish fillet 140 g
2 large onions, thinly sliced
2 crushed garlic cloves and ground cumin 1 tsp
Ground coriander half a tsp and a pinch of ground cinnamon
White rice 110 g and light fish or vegetable stock 200 ml
Lemon juice, salt and black pepper
Brown the onion in a dry pan over medium-low heat 15-18 minutes, stirring, until it turns dark and sweet.
Divide the browned onion in half, mash one half and set aside for garnish.
Cook the rice with half the mashed onion, garlic, cumin, coriander, cinnamon and stock until fully cooked.
Season the fish with salt, black pepper and lemon juice, bake at 200°C for 15-18 minutes, serve over the rice and garnish with the remaining browned onion.

name.en: Chicken and Yogurt Rice (Levantine Comfort Bowl)

en: Cooked, shredded chicken breast 140 g
Cooked white rice 110 g
Low-fat Greek yogurt 100 g
1 crushed garlic clove and tahini 1 tsp
Toasted pine nuts 1 tbsp (optional)
Salt, black pepper and a pinch of dried mint
Mix the yogurt with the garlic, tahini and salt until combined.
Place the rice on a serving plate, add the shredded chicken over it.
Pour the yogurt sauce over the chicken and rice.
Sprinkle with black pepper and dried mint, garnish with pine nuts if desired and serve.

name.en: Freekeh Soup with Chicken

en: Washed freekeh 50 g
Chicken breast, small cubes, 100 g
Chopped onion and 1 crushed garlic clove
Ground cumin half a tsp and a pinch of ground cinnamon
Light vegetable stock 600 ml
Salt, black pepper and a little lemon juice to serve
Brown the onion and garlic in a dry pot for 3 minutes.
Add the chicken and stir until it changes colour.
Add the freekeh, cumin, cinnamon and stock, cover and simmer 25-30 minutes until the freekeh and chicken are fully cooked.
Adjust the salt and black pepper, serve hot with a little lemon juice.

name.en: Batata bil Furn (Baked Potato and Chicken Tray)

en: Potato, cubed, 200 g
Chicken breast, cubed, 140 g
Diced tomato and 2 crushed garlic cloves
Mixed spice half a tsp and chopped fresh coriander
Light vegetable stock 150 ml and 1 tsp oil
Salt and black pepper
Mix the potato and chicken with the tomato, garlic, mixed spice, salt and black pepper in a baking dish.
Drizzle the oil and stock over it.
Cover the dish with foil and bake at 220°C for 30 minutes.
Remove the foil and bake for another 15-20 minutes until the potato and chicken are fully cooked and the top is golden, garnish with fresh coriander and serve.

name.en: Aubergine moussaka

en: 1 large aubergine, sliced
120 g lean minced meat
1 onion and 2 tomatoes
1 garlic clove, cinnamon
1 tbsp oil, salt
Roast the aubergine slices in the oven 15 minutes
Brown the meat with the onion and garlic
Add the tomato and cinnamon, cook 10 minutes
Layer in a baking dish and bake 20 minutes

name.en: Light chicken and aubergine maqluba

en: 150 g chicken breast, cubed
100 g basmati rice
1 roasted aubergine, sliced
1 carrot, a little cauliflower
Maqluba spice (turmeric, cinnamon, cardamom)
Brown the chicken with the spice 5 minutes
Layer aubergine, then chicken, then vegetables in a pot
Add the rice on top with water just covering it
Cook 25 minutes, then flip onto a serving plate

name.en: Baked Kibbeh bil Sanieh (Layered Bulgur and Meat Bake)

en: Fine bulgur, soaked 10 minutes, 120 g
Lean minced beef 140 g (divided into two portions)
Grated onion and finely chopped onion
Mixed spice and ground cumin half a tsp each
Toasted pine nuts 1 tbsp (optional)
2 tsp oil, salt and black pepper
Grind half the meat with the soaked bulgur, grated onion and mixed spice in a food processor until a smooth, cohesive dough forms.
Brown the chopped onion in a dry pan for 3 minutes, add the other half of the meat and stir until cooked, add the cumin, salt, black pepper and pine nuts if desired.
Spread half the bulgur dough in the bottom of a small greased baking dish, spread the meat filling over it, cover with the other half of the bulgur dough and press gently.
Score diagonal lines on the surface with a knife, brush with oil, and bake at 220°C for 25-30 minutes until the top is golden and crisp, cut into squares and serve.

name.en: Baked Kofta bil Tahini (Meatballs in Tahini Sauce)

en: Lean minced beef 140 g
Grated onion and chopped parsley
Mixed spice half a tsp, salt and black pepper
Tahini 2 tbsp and lemon juice 1 tbsp
Warm water about 80 ml and 1 crushed garlic clove for the sauce
Toasted pine nuts for garnish (optional)
Knead the minced beef thoroughly with the grated onion, parsley, mixed spice, salt and black pepper until it binds together.
Shape into small balls, arrange on a lined tray, bake at 220°C for 12-15 minutes until nearly cooked.
Mix the tahini, lemon juice and garlic with the warm water gradually until you get a smooth, pourable sauce.
Pour the tahini sauce over the kofta, return to the oven for another 5-7 minutes until fully cooked and the sauce sets slightly, garnish with pine nuts if desired and serve.

name.en: Baked Chicken Shawarma with Rice

en: Chicken breast, sliced, 140 g
2 crushed garlic cloves and lemon juice 2 tbsp
Ground cumin, ground coriander and paprika half a tsp each
White vinegar 1 tsp and 1 tsp oil
Salt and black pepper
Cooked white rice 110 g
Mix the garlic, lemon juice, cumin, coriander, paprika, vinegar, salt and black pepper to make the marinade.
Rub the chicken with it and let it sit at least 30 minutes or overnight in the fridge.
Arrange on a lined tray and brush with oil.
Bake at 220°C for 18-20 minutes, turning halfway, until fully cooked and the edges turn golden, and serve with the rice.

name.en: Baked Samak Harra (Spicy Levantine Fish) with Rice

en: White fish fillet 140 g
3 crushed garlic cloves and chopped fresh coriander
Chopped hot chili (optional) and lemon juice 2 tbsp
Ground cumin half a tsp and 1 tsp olive oil
Salt and black pepper
Cooked white rice 110 g
Mix the garlic, fresh coriander, hot chili if desired, lemon juice, cumin, olive oil, salt and black pepper to make the marinade paste.
Rub the fish thoroughly with the paste and let it sit 15-20 minutes.
Arrange on a lined tray.
Bake at 200°C for 18-20 minutes until fully cooked, and serve with the rice.

name.en: Baked Kibbeh bil Laban (Kibbeh in Yogurt Sauce)

en: Fine bulgur, soaked 10 minutes, 80 g
Lean minced beef 120 g
Grated onion and mixed spice half a tsp
Low-fat Greek yogurt 200 g for the sauce
1 crushed garlic clove and cornflour half a tsp for the sauce
A pinch of dried mint, salt and black pepper
Grind the meat with the soaked bulgur, grated onion, mixed spice, salt and black pepper in a food processor until a smooth, cohesive dough forms.
Shape into small balls, arrange on a lined tray, bake at 220°C for 15-18 minutes until golden.
Dissolve the cornflour in a little yogurt, add it to the rest of the yogurt with the garlic and salt, heat in a small pot over low heat, stirring, until it thickens slightly without boiling.
Pour the yogurt sauce over the kibbeh, sprinkle with dried mint and serve.

name.en: Grilled Kafta Skewers with Rice

en: Lean minced beef 140 g
Grated onion and chopped parsley
Mixed spice half a tsp and mild hot pepper (optional)
Salt, black pepper and 1 tsp oil
Wooden skewers soaked in water
Cooked white rice 110 g
Knead the minced beef with the grated onion, parsley, mixed spice, hot pepper if desired, salt and black pepper thoroughly until it binds together.
Shape into long fingers around the wooden skewers.
Arrange on a lined tray and brush with oil.
Grill under the broiler or in a 220°C oven for 15-18 minutes, turning halfway, until fully cooked, and serve with the rice.

name.en: Baked Samak bi Tahini (Fish with Tahini Sauce) with Rice

en: White fish fillet 140 g
Tahini 2 tbsp and lemon juice 2 tbsp
1 crushed garlic clove and warm water about 60 ml
Onion, thinly sliced and browned in a dry pan (optional for garnish)
Salt and black pepper
Cooked white rice 110 g
Season the fish with salt and black pepper, bake at 200°C for 15-18 minutes until fully cooked.
Mix the tahini, lemon juice and garlic with the warm water gradually until you get a smooth, pourable sauce.
Pour the tahini sauce over the baked fish.
Garnish with the browned onion if desired, and serve with the rice.

name.en: Grilled Lamb Kofta with Freekeh

en: Lean minced lamb 130 g
Grated onion and chopped parsley
Mixed spice half a tsp and a pinch of ground cumin
Salt, black pepper and 1 tsp oil
Cooked freekeh 110 g
Wooden skewers soaked in water
Knead the minced lamb thoroughly with the grated onion, parsley, mixed spice, cumin, salt and black pepper until it binds together.
Shape into long fingers around the wooden skewers.
Arrange on a lined tray and brush with oil.
Grill under the broiler or in a 220°C oven for 15-18 minutes, turning halfway, until fully cooked, and serve with the freekeh.

name.en: Moutabbal aubergine dip

en: 1 large aubergine
2 tbsp tahini
Lemon juice, 1 crushed garlic clove
1 tsp olive oil
Pomegranate and parsley to garnish
Roast the whole aubergine over a flame or in the oven until soft inside
Peel and mash the flesh
Mix it with the tahini, lemon and garlic
Garnish with oil, pomegranate and parsley

name.en: Zaatar labneh balls

en: 100 g strained low-fat labneh
1 tsp dried thyme mix
1 tsp olive oil
A pinch of sumac
Vegetable sticks to serve
Shape the labneh into small balls with wet hands
Roll them in the thyme mix
Arrange on a plate and drizzle with oil and sumac
Serve with the vegetable sticks

name.en: Baked Sfiha (Mini Meat Pies with Tomato)

en: Lean minced beef 100 g
Diced tomato and chopped onion
Mixed spice and ground sumac (optional) half a tsp each
Toasted pine nuts 1 tbsp (optional)
Ready-made whole-wheat bread dough 80 g
Salt and black pepper
Mix the minced meat with the tomato, onion, mixed spice, sumac, salt and black pepper until combined.
Divide the dough into 6 small balls, roll into thin circles.
Place a spoonful of filling in the centre of each circle and spread with your finger to cover most of the disc, add pine nuts if desired.
Arrange on a lined tray, bake at 220°C for 15-18 minutes until the meat is cooked and the pastry turns golden.

name.en: Warak Enab (Stuffed Grape Leaves with Rice)

en: Canned grape leaves, drained, 12 leaves
Egyptian or short-grain rice 80 g
Diced tomato and chopped parsley
Chopped fresh mint and lemon juice 2 tbsp
1 tsp olive oil, salt and black pepper
Light vegetable stock 200 ml
Mix the rice with the tomato, parsley, mint, lemon juice, olive oil, salt and black pepper.
Spread out a grape leaf, place a teaspoon of filling at the base, fold in the sides and roll tightly.
Repeat with the remaining leaves, arrange them snugly in a pot, one on top of another.
Pour the stock over them, cover and simmer 35-40 minutes until the rice is fully cooked, and serve warm.

name.en: Baked Fatayer Sabanekh (Spinach Hand Pies)

en: Fresh spinach, chopped and well drained, 200 g
Chopped onion and lemon juice 2 tbsp
Ground sumac half a tsp and 1 tsp olive oil
Toasted pine nuts 1 tbsp (optional)
Ready-made whole-wheat bread dough 80 g
Salt and black pepper
Squeeze the chopped spinach thoroughly to remove as much moisture as possible.
Mix it with the onion, lemon juice, sumac, olive oil, salt and black pepper, add pine nuts if desired.
Divide the dough into 6 small balls, roll into thin circles, place a spoonful of filling in the centre of each circle and fold the three edges to form a sealed triangle.
Arrange on a lined tray, bake at 220°C for 15-18 minutes until golden and crisp.

name.en: Baked Halloumi and Za'atar Bites

en: Low-salt halloumi cheese, cut into pieces, 140 g
Dried thyme (zaatar) 1 tbsp
Lemon juice 1 tbsp and 1 tsp olive oil
6 cherry tomatoes to serve (optional)
Fresh mint for garnish (optional)
Black pepper
Brush the halloumi pieces with olive oil and sprinkle with thyme and black pepper.
Arrange on a lined tray.
Bake at 220°C for 10-12 minutes, turning halfway, until golden on the outside.
Sprinkle with lemon juice after removing, serve with cherry tomatoes and mint if desired.

name.en: Baked Lahm bi Ajeen (Mini Meat-Topped Flatbread)

en: Lean minced beef 80 g
Diced tomato and chopped onion
Chopped green bell pepper and 1 crushed garlic clove
Mixed spice half a tsp and pomegranate molasses 1 tsp (optional)
Ready-made whole-wheat bread dough 80 g
Salt and black pepper
Mix the minced meat with the tomato, onion, bell pepper, garlic, mixed spice, pomegranate molasses if desired, salt and black pepper until combined.
Divide the dough into 6 small balls, roll into thin circles.
Place a spoonful of filling in the centre of each circle and spread with your finger to cover most of the disc.
Arrange on a lined tray, bake at 220°C for 15-18 minutes until the meat is cooked and the pastry turns golden.

name.en: Za'atar Roasted Chickpeas

en: Canned chickpeas, drained and dried well, 200 g
1 tsp olive oil
Dried thyme (zaatar) 1 tbsp
A little salt
A little lemon juice after roasting
A pinch of black pepper
Dry the chickpeas thoroughly with a paper towel to remove as much moisture as possible.
Mix them with the oil, thyme and salt.
Arrange in a single layer on a lined tray.
Bake at 200°C for 30-35 minutes, stirring every 10 minutes, until fully crisp, sprinkle with lemon juice and black pepper after removing and serve once slightly cooled.

name.en: Baked Kibbeh Kraaz (Bulgur and Meat Torpedo Bites)

en: Fine bulgur, soaked 10 minutes, 80 g
Lean minced beef 120 g (divided into two portions)
Grated onion and finely chopped onion
Mixed spice and ground cumin half a tsp each
Toasted pine nuts 1 tbsp (optional)
Salt, black pepper and 1 tsp oil
Grind half the meat with the soaked bulgur, grated onion and mixed spice in a food processor until a smooth, cohesive dough forms.
Brown the chopped onion in a dry pan for 3 minutes, add the other half of the meat and stir until cooked, add the cumin, salt, black pepper and pine nuts if desired.
Take a small amount of the bulgur dough, shape into a ball and press with your finger to form a hollow, fill with the meat filling and seal into a small tapered torpedo shape.
Arrange on a lined tray, brush with oil, and bake at 220°C for 16-18 minutes, turning halfway, until golden and crisp.

name.en: Baked Rekakat bi Jibn (Thin Cheese Rolls)

en: Low-fat cottage cheese 100 g
Low-fat grated mozzarella 40 g
Chopped parsley and chopped fresh mint
1 egg
Thin whole-wheat pastry sheets, 4 pieces (60 g)
Egg white for brushing, salt and black pepper
Mix the cottage cheese and mozzarella with the parsley, mint, egg, salt and black pepper until combined.
Place two tablespoons of filling along the edge of each pastry sheet and roll tightly into a thin cylinder, seal the edge with egg white.
Arrange on a lined tray and brush with egg white.
Bake at 220°C for 15-18 minutes, turning halfway, until golden and crisp.

name.en: Light ashta with fruit

en: 1 cup low-fat milk
2 tbsp cornstarch
1 tsp orange blossom water and honey
Chopped seasonal fruit
A few crushed pistachios
Dissolve the cornstarch in a quarter cup of cold milk
Heat the rest of the milk and add the cornstarch mix
Stir on low heat until it thickens, then add the blossom water and honey
Chill, top with fruit and sprinkle the pistachios

name.en: Light baked namoura

en: Half cup coarse semolina
2 tbsp Greek yogurt
1 tsp baking powder, cardamom
1 tsp honey in the batter
1 almond to garnish + a light sugar syrup
Mix the semolina, yogurt, baking powder, cardamom and honey
Pour into a small greased tin
Place the almond in the centre and bake 20 minutes at 180°C
Pour the light syrup over it while hot

name.en: Baked Maamoul (Date-Filled Semolina Cookies)

en: Semolina 60 g
Melted low-fat butter 2 tbsp
Warm water about 30 ml and brown sugar 1 tsp
Pitted dates, mashed, 50 g for the filling
A pinch of ground cinnamon for the filling
A pinch of powdered sugar for garnish (optional)
Mix the semolina with the melted butter until fully absorbed, let it rest 30 minutes.
Gradually add the warm water and brown sugar and knead until a soft, cohesive dough forms.
Mix the mashed dates with the cinnamon for the filling.

Shape the dough into small balls, press each ball to form a hollow, fill with dates and seal, flatten slightly, arrange on a lined tray, bake at 180°C for 18-20 minutes until golden on the bottom, dust with powdered sugar if desired once cooled.

name.en: Muhallabia (Levantine Milk Pudding with Orange Blossom and Pistachio)

en: Low-fat milk 350 ml
Cornflour 2 tbsp
Brown sugar 25 g
Orange blossom water 1 tsp
Coarsely chopped pistachios 1 tbsp for garnish
A pinch of salt
Dissolve the cornflour in a quarter cup of the cold milk until smooth without lumps.
Heat the remaining milk with the brown sugar and salt in a pot over medium heat until nearly boiling.
Gradually stir in the cornflour mixture, stirring constantly, cook 5-7 minutes until the texture thickens like a creamy pudding.
Remove from the heat and add the orange blossom water, pour into serving cups, chill in the fridge for at least 2 hours, sprinkle with pistachios before serving.

name.en: Baked Qatayef (Stuffed Sweet Pancakes, Levantine Style)

en: Whole-wheat flour 60 g
Warm water about 90 ml and a pinch of instant yeast
Brown sugar 1 tsp for the batter
Coarsely ground walnuts 30 g for the filling
A pinch of ground cinnamon and brown sugar 1 tsp for the filling
Honey or light sugar syrup 1 tbsp to serve
Mix the flour with the warm water, yeast and brown sugar gradually until a smooth liquid batter forms, let it rest 20-30 minutes until small bubbles appear.
Heat a non-stick pan, pour a tablespoon of batter to form a small disc, cook on one side only until bubbles appear and the surface dries, do not flip.
Repeat with the remaining batter, mix the walnuts with the cinnamon and brown sugar for the filling.

Place a spoonful of filling on the uncooked side of each disc, fold in half and press the edges to seal like a clamshell, arrange on a lined tray and bake at 200°C for 15-18 minutes until golden, pour honey over them while hot and serve.

name.en: Baked Barazek (Sesame and Pistachio Cookies)

en: Whole-wheat flour 60 g
Melted low-fat butter 2 tbsp
Brown sugar 25 g and warm water 1 tbsp
A pinch of baking powder
Sesame seeds 20 g for coating
Coarsely chopped pistachios 1 tbsp for coating
Mix the flour with the melted butter, brown sugar, warm water and baking powder until a soft, cohesive dough forms.
Shape into small flat discs.
Dip one side of each disc in the sesame seeds and the other in the chopped pistachios, press gently to adhere.
Arrange on a lined tray, bake at 180°C for 15-18 minutes until golden, let cool before serving to become crisp.

name.en: Baked Halawet el Jibn (Sweet Cheese Rolls with Rosewater)

en: Semolina 40 g and water 150 ml
Brown sugar 20 g and rosewater 1 tsp
Low-fat cottage cheese 80 g
Low-fat cream or thick Greek yogurt 40 g for the filling
Coarsely chopped pistachios for garnish
Light sugar syrup 1 tbsp to serve
Cook the semolina with the water and brown sugar in a small pot over medium heat, stirring constantly, 5-7 minutes until the texture thickens like a dough.
Add the cottage cheese and rosewater, mix well over low heat for two minutes until the mixture is smooth and slightly stretchy.
While warm, spread the mixture on a surface moistened with a little water into a thin layer, place the cream along one edge and roll tightly into a cylinder.
Let it cool, then cut into small pieces, sprinkle with pistachios and pour the sugar syrup over them, and serve cold.

name.en: Baked Znoud el Sit (Cream-Filled Pastry Rolls)

en: Low-fat cream or thick Greek yogurt 80 g
Powdered sugar 1 tsp and orange blossom water half a tsp for the filling
Thin whole-wheat pastry sheets, 4 pieces (60 g)
Melted low-fat butter 1 tsp for brushing
Light sugar syrup 1 tbsp to serve
Coarsely chopped pistachios for garnish
Mix the cream with the powdered sugar and orange blossom water for the filling.
Cut each pastry sheet into long strips, place a teaspoon of filling at one end and roll tightly into a thin cylinder.
Arrange on a lined tray and brush with the melted butter.
Bake at 220°C for 12-15 minutes, turning halfway, until golden and crisp, pour the sugar syrup over them, sprinkle with pistachios and serve.

name.en: Baked Osmaliyeh (Crispy Shredded Pastry with Cream)

en: Thin kunafa shreds 60 g
Melted low-fat butter 2 tbsp
Low-fat cream or thick Greek yogurt 80 g for the filling
Powdered sugar 1 tsp and a pinch of orange blossom water for the filling
Light sugar syrup 2 tbsp to serve
Coarsely chopped pistachios for garnish
Rub the kunafa shreds with your hands to loosen them, mix with the melted butter until fully coated.
Place half the shreds in a small greased tin and press evenly.
Mix the cream with the powdered sugar and orange blossom water, spread over the first layer of shreds, cover with the other half of the shreds and press gently.
Bake at 200°C for 20-25 minutes until golden and crisp, pour the sugar syrup over it while hot, sprinkle with pistachios and serve warm.

name.en: Baked Ghraybeh (Shortbread Cookies)

en: Whole-wheat flour 70 g
Melted low-fat butter 3 tbsp
Powdered sugar 25 g
Vanilla extract half a tsp
Whole blanched almonds, 6 pieces for garnish (optional)
A pinch of salt
Mix the melted butter with the powdered sugar until well combined.
Add the vanilla, salt and flour gradually and knead gently until a soft, cohesive dough forms (do not overwork it).
Shape into small balls, place one almond on top of each ball if desired, press gently.
Arrange on a lined tray, bake at 170°C for 16-18 minutes without letting them colour much, let cool completely before serving to become crisp.
